tells: 1. Face close is unmistakably a game-character head: waxy uniform orange skin with no pores, specular or subsurface variation, painted-on eyebrows, eyes with flat glassy whites and baked catchlights that don't match any light in the room, and a frozen half-smile mouth (club-4-face.png, centre face)

2. Lighting is unmotivated: front row is evenly lit from the camera position with no visible source, while the 'candle' cups on the tables are pink emissive blobs that throw no warm uplight onto hands, faces or the table tops (club-1-wide.png and club-3-mid.png, table cups and front-row faces)

3. Back of house is a stamped wall of identical flat black cut-out silhouettes standing in haze with no rim light, no colour, no depth falloff and no seats; reads as a cardboard backdrop (club-1-wide.png, upper-middle band; club-2-mid.png, upper left)

4. Contact and grounding: tables float with no contact shadow or occlusion, hands rest on/through table edges, chairs are dark shapes people hover in front of, and nobody casts a shadow on floor or table (club-3-mid.png, centre table and the green-hoodie man's hands; club-1-wide.png, floor under tables)

5. Motion strip shows mostly rigid people: only 2-3 heads turn while torsos, shoulders and the rest of the row stay locked; the 'laugh' onset has no breath, shoulder lift or lean, and mouths open without the face changing (club-5-strip.png, all six frames, front row)

1. The whole auditorium is exposed like a flat ambient fill with no stage spill falloff: rows four and five back are as bright as row one, faces have no key/fill direction, and the back rows sit upright like mannequins on a grid (theatre-1-wide.png, entire middle band)

2. Contact failure: people float in front of the red seats instead of sinking into them, legs and knees clip/hover, nobody's back touches a seatback and there is no occlusion where bodies meet chairs (theatre-1-wide.png, front row legs; theatre-3-mid.png, front row)

3. Face close: plasticky blonde head with smeared low-res hair texture, painted-on stubble-like hairline, dead eyes with no wetness, and a mouth that opens like a hinge into a dark void with no tongue or teeth detail (theatre-4-face.png, centre face and mouth)

4. Clones and posing: identical ram-rod postures with hands on knees across rows, repeated characters (same pink tank top, same teal hoodie man appearing in every venue), and an obvious stretched/transparent artefact on the second-row figure's arm (theatre-2-mid.png, behind the blonde woman at centre; theatre-6-held.png, centre)

5. Strip motion is minimal and asynchronous in a fake way: a couple of heads tilt and one mouth opens while 30+ visible people stay frozen at the onset of a laugh; no shoulder shake, no collective response (theatre-5-strip.png, all frames, rows 2-4)

1. Face close: CG young man with smooth airbrushed skin, uniformly lit, sharp cut-out jaw edge against the blur, hair that is a solid helmet with a ragged alpha fringe and black blob behind the ear, and pale grey eyes with no reflection of the room (openmic-4-face.png, centre head and right ear)

2. Front row lit like a softbox from camera with the warm spill wrapping evenly over every person; the row of practical ceiling spots overhead is visible but throws no top light or hair rim, so the light has no source (openmic-1-wide.png, front row vs ceiling lights)

3. Grounding: people sit on nothing visible, chairs mostly missing or swallowed by black, legs hang into a void and no floor shadows exist; the front row reads as composited onto black (openmic-1-wide.png, lower half; openmic-6-held.png, right side legs and feet)

4. Faces lit with the same flat exposure regardless of depth; blacked-out lips and gums on the two women read as texture errors, and teeth look painted (openmic-2-mid.png, the green-top and hoodie women's mouths)

5. Motion strip: heads swivel on stiff necks and mouths open while bodies, hands and shoulders stay locked to the knees; no breathing, no weight shift, so the laugh onset reads as puppetry (openmic-5-strip.png, frames 12.6-13.0, centre group)
